headline: Medium risk: shared document workflows can leak or mis-handle sensitive support data, while prompt-injection and capability-conflict risks are limited by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee can ingest documents and session memory, while pdf.js processes PDF files in a browser-based worker model. A prompt-injection path exists only if PDF content from pdf.js is manually or programmatically fed into cognee as trusted instructions; no shared channel is documented, so the pathway is limited and indirect.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into cognee as instruction-bearing text without sanitization, injection risk exists.
IF both agents are connected through a shared file or clipboard bridge, attacker-controlled PDF text can influence cognee.
mitigations: Require explicit human review before importing PDF-derived text into cognee.
Strip instruction-like text from PDFs before downstream use.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Disable any automatic copy/paste or file-watching bridge between them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches customer support data, personal data, finance data, and documents, while pdf.js opens PDF files locally with no network egress. If the same PDFs or exported support artifacts flow from cognee into pdf.js, sensitive content can be exposed in a shared workspace; the risk is real in default document-processing workflows, though pdf.js itself is not a network exfiltrator.
conditions: IF cognee exports sensitive support documents into a workspace readable by pdf.js, those contents are exposed to the PDF renderer.
IF the operator opens customer or finance PDFs in pdf.js that originated from cognee, sensitive data is duplicated across tools.
mitigations: Keep cognee and pdf.js on separate directories.
Open only redacted PDFs in pdf.js.
Turn off any shared sync folder between the tools.
Delete temporary exports immediately after review.
Use least-privilege file permissions on the document workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, but cognee only advertises allowlisted network egress and pdf.js has no network egress. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is not evidenced; uncertainty remains because filesystem locking details are absent.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file-level conflicts can occur.
IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple operator workflow.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
Use read-only mounts for pdf.js when possible.

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, while pdf.js is a document-processing worker that can render those outputs. If pdf.js content is treated as authoritative downstream, errors or hallucinated structure from cognee can cascade into rendered documents or operator actions; the pair lacks a documented verification step, so the pathway is plausible in default document pipelines.
conditions: IF pdf.js is used to render cognee-generated documents without verification, downstream users may trust incorrect content.
IF cognee outputs are copied into operational documents, errors can propagate into later actions.
mitigations: Add a human verification step before publishing rendered documents.
Mark cognee outputs as untrusted until checked.
Compare rendered PDFs against source text for critical fields.
Restrict pdf.js to viewing only, not approval workflows.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while pdf.js handles PDF documents locally. If regulated support artifacts are opened in pdf.js after being processed by cognee, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the pair; no specific certification mismatch is documented, so this is a policy-gap risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated customer documents are processed by cognee and then stored or viewed in pdf.js, retention policy alignment is required.
IF the operator uses the pair on EU personal data or finance data, residency and logging controls must be checked.
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for both tools.
Avoid storing regulated PDFs in shared temp folders.
Use separate deletion policies for exports and views.
Review whether the workflow handles personal or finance data before use.
